author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing opens the first page when asked for a page below the first
summary: A request for the owner listing with a page number below the first currently renders the error page. It must list the first page of results instead. Requests for the first page or a later one keep their present behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given a request for the owner listing with a page number below the first, when the listing runs, then the first page of results is listed.
Given a request for the owner listing with a page number below the first, when the listing runs, then the error page is not shown.
Given a request for the owner listing with the first page or a later one, when the listing runs, then that page is listed unchanged.
Given a page number of zero and a negative page number, when the listing runs for each, then both open the first page.
non_goals: Page values that are not numbers — the owner's report bounds itself to values below the first page.
Page values beyond the last page — unstated in the report and unchanged by this slice.
The veterinarian directory's paging — outside the report; recorded as an open question in the PRD.
notes: Grounded solely in the intake-decision at handoff.jsonl line 1; no further owner decisions were recorded. Scope is the owner listing only. PRD updated: REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001 added to the Owner records narrative with three Done-when bullets and edge case 4. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. Two adjacent gaps recorded under Open Questions rather than decided here.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice adjusts the existing owner-listing pagination helper in OwnerController; no new type, package, or dependency. It sits on the pattern catalog's Web controller row in architecture-principles.md: binding a request parameter into a page number is HTTP-surface adaptation, not a business rule, so the standing controller deviation is not widened. security-principles.md Trust Boundaries places range checking where external input arrives; the PRD's contract admits a page below the first and maps it to the first page rather than rejecting it. Recorded in system-design.md Contracts under 'Invariants the rows cannot carry'. Basis: grep over OwnerController.java, VetController.java, and owners/ownersList.html (IDE oracle not connected; weaker than symbol resolution).
integration_points: OwnerController.processFindForm binds the page request parameter and passes it to both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel
addPaginationModel publishes currentPage, which owners/ownersList.html uses to build the first, previous, next, and last links

patterns.description: existing findPaginatedForOwnersLastName helper converting a one-based page into a zero-based PageRequest
external input is bounded where it arrives; internal code past the boundary trusts its contracts

risks.risk: Bounding only inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName leaves the unbounded value in the currentPage model attribute, so ownersList.html builds paging links from it (currentPage + 1 from -3 yields page -2) and re-enters the defect one click later.
risks.mitigation: Bound the page once where the request parameter enters processFindForm, then pass the single bounded value to both the query helper and addPaginationModel.

risks.risk: VetController carries the identical PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) shape and stays unbounded, so the two listings diverge.
risks.mitigation: Out of scope by the prd-entry's non-goals; the divergence is now stated in system-design.md and the vet gap remains the PRD's open question. Do not extract a shared helper in this slice.

notes: Five-signal foundational check: no signal trips. Architecture shape, framework, persistence, and error-flow patterns are all recorded; ubiquitous-language is populated and confirmed. No design-doc-autofix records exist since the last design-block, so the autofix audit is empty. Durable-memory write: one paragraph added to system-design.md Contracts stating the owner listing's page bound and the vet listing's absence of one. No ADR — the choice is neither hard to reverse nor a real trade-off; the PRD already fixed the behavior. Rejection was the alternative and the requirement rules it out. No new domain term enters the vocabulary: 'page' and 'listing' are presentation words, not domain concepts.

author: feature-implementer
summary: OwnerController.processFindForm now bounds the incoming page parameter once at its entry point with Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) and passes the single bounded value to both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, so a page below the first lists the first page (HTTP 200) and the currentPage model attribute the ownersList paging links are built from can never carry an out-of-range value. Two parameterized tests added to OwnerControllerTests: theOwnerListingShouldTreatAPageBelowTheFirstAsTheFirstPage over page 0 and -3 (was red with IllegalArgumentException from PageRequest.of), and theOwnerListingShouldOpenTheRequestedPageWhenItIsTheFirstOrLater over pages 1 and 2 as the unchanged-behaviour guard. VetController left untouched per the recorded non-goal; no shared helper extracted. IDE static-analysis pre-check not run (IDE not consulted). No configuration properties changed.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The local variable `requestedPage` actually holds the bounded/clamped page (Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE)), while the still-in-scope method parameter `page` holds the raw, unbounded value the client requested. The names read backwards: a future reader skimming past the comment will expect `requestedPage` to mean 'what the client asked for' and `page` to mean nothing in particular — exactly inverted from reality. This is the kind of local mis-naming that survives refactors because it still compiles and passes tests.
findings.fix: Rename `requestedPage` to something that names the post-bound value, e.g. `boundedPage` or `effectivePage` (and correspondingly in the two call sites at lines 113 and 127).

approved_aspects: The bound is applied once at the entry point (processFindForm) and the single bounded value flows to both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, matching the design-block's stated risk mitigation and avoiding the currentPage-drift defect the design-block called out.
FIRST_PAGE is a well-named constant replacing a magic literal, with a short comment explaining the rationale for the bound.
checkFormat passes; no formatting violations in the diff.

The two new parameterized MockMvc tests are named descriptively (BDD-style) and use ValueSource to cover the boundary (0, -3) and the unchanged-behavior guard (1, 2) without duplicating near-identical test methods.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain was not verified against the NVD in this review: build.gradle declares no OWASP dependency-check plugin (grep for dependencyCheck/owasp returns nothing) and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match ran. The change set touches no build file, so the resolved dependency set is unchanged from the last reviewed state; the resolved framework floor is Spring Boot 4.1.0 with io.spring.dependency-management 1.1.7. Closing the CVE check needs CI or a human, and is not this slice's work.

No upper bound on page. A request such as /owners?page=2000000000 still reaches PageRequest.of(1999999999, 5) and issues a query with an offset near 1e10, which some vendors scan for. This is pre-existing, untouched by the change, already recorded as a PRD non-goal ('page values beyond the last page') and as an open question, so it is not a finding here — but it is the remaining half of the same boundary check and is worth a future slice.

VetController carries the identical unbounded PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) shape. The pattern-consistency divergence is justified in durable memory (docs/system-design.md Contracts states the owner listing's bound and the vet listing's absence of one, and the PRD carries it as an open question), so it is documented rather than silent; the code itself carries no pointer, which is acceptable given the docs entry.
approved_aspects: Input validation sits at the trust boundary: the page parameter is bounded once in processFindForm where the request enters, and the single bounded value flows to both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel. This matches docs/security-principles.md Trust Boundaries ('validate type, range and shape before use') and leaves no unbounded copy behind the boundary.

Integer-underflow path removed. Before the change, page = Integer.MIN_VALUE reached findPaginatedForOwnersLastName, where page - 1 wraps to Integer.MAX_VALUE and PageRequest.of builds an offset near 1.07e10; the clamp makes that path unreachable. Every other value below 1 previously reached PageRequest.of and threw, surfacing the framework exception on the error page.

Thymeleaf preprocessing in owners/ownersList.html (lines 44, 49, 54) evaluates __${currentPage - 1}__ / __${currentPage + 1}__. currentPage is now guaranteed >= 1, so the generated paging links can no longer carry an out-of-range page back to the same endpoint. The value is an int bound by Spring type conversion, so no request-supplied text can reach the preprocessing slot; the change narrows this surface rather than widening it.

No new attack surface: no route added, no file or process operation, no shell execution, no serialization, no reflection, no logging. Data access remains Spring Data derived queries with no string-concatenated query text (grep over the changed controller for Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec/Files./FileWriter//tmp//createQuery/new Random returns nothing).
No secrets introduced. grep over both changed Java files for password/secret/token/api-key/credential returns nothing; build.gradle and the profile property files are untouched by the change set.
No mutable state added to the singleton controller: FIRST_PAGE is a static final int and requestedPage is a method-local, so the clamp is thread-safe under concurrent requests.

Baseline comparison per docs/security-principles.md 'Applying this section': the change introduces none of the ten vulnerability classes in the Realization table and leaves the application no weaker than the docs/system-design.md Security Context baseline.
